name: p50
about: The average adult man the robolab bodies already model (body.py): every multiplier 1.0, so ROBOLAB_PROFILE=p50 builds byte-identical XML to no profile. Listed so a percentile profile has an explicit reference, and so the reference's own calibration and its known departures from population means are written down in one place.
population: healthy young adult men (the body.py calibration)

strength.stat: peak isometric joint torque of the average young man (body.py LEG_JOINTS / V2_MONO_PEAKS / V2_BIARTICULAR peaks, strength 1.0)
strength.note: Per-joint peaks: knee extension 230 + 0.8 x 150 = 350 N m (vasti + rectus femoris), plantarflexion 150 + 180 = 330 N m, hip extension 100 + 200 = 300 N m (v2). These sit at the high end of isometric means for young men (knee extension ~250-300 N m) because the model's peaks are MuJoCo peak isometric forces at optimal length, not dynamometer values.

speed.stat: unloaded peak joint angular velocity (body.py V2_OMEGA: hip 15, knee 25, ankle 20 rad/s ...)

tendon.stat: v3 series-elastic tendons: Achilles 200 N/mm at 5.0 cm, quadriceps 250 N/mm at 4.5 cm (body.py V3_TENDONS)

activation.stat: MuJoCo muscle timeconst 10 ms activation / 40 ms deactivation

anthro.stat: 1.75 m stature, 67.5 kg (segment lengths and masses after Winter's tables)
anthro.note: 1.75 m is the young-adult male mean stature (ANSUR II / NHANES ~1.75-1.76 m). 67.5 kg (BMI 22) is a lean build, below the current US male mean mass (~85-90 kg, BMI ~27-29); the percentile profiles scale this lean build at constant BMI rather than adopting the population's mean mass.
